description: Candidate stories parked for future consideration. These were de-scoped in favor of higher-impact user-visible features.

stories.title: Export dependency graph as Graphviz DOT file for advanced rendering
stories.description: Mermaid covers basic graph needs but large PRDs with 100+ stories render poorly in it. Add a --format dot flag to spiral graph that outputs a Graphviz DOT file with cluster subgraphs grouping stories by priority tier. DOT files can be rendered by graphviz dot CLI or imported into draw.io for publication-quality diagrams.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral graph --format dot produces a valid DOT digraph consumable by graphviz dot -Tsvg
Nodes are coloured by status: pending=white, in_progress=yellow, passed=green, failed=red
Priority clusters group nodes: subgraph cluster_critical, cluster_high, cluster_medium, cluster_low
The output DOT file passes dot -Tsvg without warnings
spiral graph --format dot | dot -Tsvg > graph.svg produces a readable SVG for a 50-story PRD
technicalNotes: Graphviz DOT language reference: https://graphviz.org/doc/info/lang.html
Use Python graphviz package for programmatic DOT generation
Node color attribute uses HTML color names compatible with both dot and neato engines

stories.title: Publish story-level OTel trace IDs to GitHub PR description
stories.description: SPIRAL creates GitHub PRs per story but the PR description currently contains no link to observability data. When OTel tracing is active and a trace ID is available for a story, append an Observability section to the PR body containing the trace ID and a direct link to the configured OTel UI (Jaeger, Zipkin, or Grafana Tempo). Closes the loop between code review and performance data.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_OTLP_UI_URL is set, generated PR descriptions include an Observability section with trace URL
Trace URL is formatted as {SPIRAL_OTLP_UI_URL}/trace/{trace_id}
If no trace ID is available the section is omitted and no placeholder is left
PR description update is idempotent: re-running on an existing PR appends only if section is absent
Integration test mocks the GitHub API and verifies the PR body contains the trace URL
technicalNotes: OTel trace ID is available from the root span context; store it to story metadata after Phase R starts
GitHub PR update uses gh pr edit --body or PATCH /repos/:owner/:repo/pulls/:pull_number
Grafana Tempo trace URL format: {tempo_host}/explore with datasource=Tempo and query=traceId

stories.title: Generate per-story ADR stub when architectural decision is detected in Phase I output
stories.description: SPIRAL's existing ADR generation is triggered globally but cannot detect when a single story makes an architectural decision. Add heuristic detection on Phase I diffs: if a new import/dependency or interface-level function signature change is found, auto-generate an ADR stub in docs/adr/ with the story ID, decision, and alternatives-considered template pre-filled from the story's technicalNotes.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase I post-processing scans the git diff for: new lines in requirements/package files, new function signatures in public module files
When heuristic fires, docs/adr/NNNN-{story-id-slug}.md is created using the MADR template format
ADR stub includes: title, date, status=proposed, context from story description, decision from technicalNotes[0], and a blank Consequences section
ADR creation is recorded as a phase event in the JSONL event log
No ADR is created when no qualifying diff patterns are detected (verified by unit test with a pure-logic diff)
technicalNotes: MADR (Markdown Architectural Decision Records) template: https://adr.github.io/madr/
Heuristic: git diff --name-only | grep -E 'requirements.txt|package.json|go.mod|Cargo.toml' or diff lines matching new function/class/export declarations
ADR numbering: count existing docs/adr/*.md files and increment by 1

stories.title: Use git sparse-checkout in worker worktrees to reduce checkout footprint for large repos
stories.description: Configure git sparse-checkout in each worker's worktree so only the files listed in the story's filesTouch hint are checked out. In large monorepos, full worktree checkout can take significant time and disk space; sparse checkout reduces both by 60-90% for stories touching a small subset of files.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_SPARSE_CHECKOUT=true and filesTouch is non-empty, worker worktrees are created with git sparse-checkout set <files>
If filesTouch is empty, sparse checkout is skipped and full checkout is used
git sparse-checkout reapply is called when the story's filesTouch list is updated
sparse-checkout mode is cone mode for performance
Feature is disabled by default (opt-in via SPIRAL_SPARSE_CHECKOUT=true)
technicalNotes: git sparse-checkout documentation: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-sparse-checkout
Cone mode is significantly faster than non-cone: use git sparse-checkout init --cone
Ensure sparse-checkout does not interfere with git worktree prune operations

stories.title: Add _humanNotes and _reviewedBy annotation fields to prd.json story schema
stories.description: Add two optional human-facing annotation fields to the prd.json story schema: _humanNotes (free-text string array for reviewer comments) and _reviewedBy (username/timestamp pairs). These fields are ignored by all automated pipeline stages but preserved through merges, giving humans a structured place to annotate stories without interfering with automation.
acceptanceCriteria: _humanNotes: string[] and _reviewedBy: {by: string, at: string}[] are valid fields in prd.json stories and pass JSON Schema validation
merge_stories.py preserves these fields when merging new research output (no clobber)
spiral export-report includes _humanNotes in the story entry if non-empty
The spiral_dashboard.py story detail view displays _humanNotes and _reviewedBy if present
These fields are stripped from the story context sent to LLM to avoid prompt contamination
technicalNotes: Add to prd.json JSON Schema file (created by the prd-schema story)
In Pydantic model, mark fields as Optional[list] = None to keep backward compatibility
Document in SPIRAL docs that underscore prefix conventionally marks non-automated fields

stories.title: Add SPIRAL_COMMIT_SIGNING env var to enable GPG/SSH signing on AI-generated commits
stories.description: Add a SPIRAL_COMMIT_SIGNING env var that, when set to gpg or ssh, configures git to sign AI-generated commits using the user's configured GPG key or SSH signing key. Signed commits provide cryptographic proof that commits attributed to the AI agent actually originated from an authorized SPIRAL run, which is important for compliance in regulated environments.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_COMMIT_SIGNING=gpg, ralph.sh passes -c commit.gpgSign=true and -c gpg.program=<gpg> to git commit
When SPIRAL_COMMIT_SIGNING=ssh, ralph.sh sets commit.gpgSign=true and gpg.format=ssh
When SPIRAL_COMMIT_SIGNING is unset or empty, signing is not configured (default behavior unchanged)
spiral-doctor verifies that the required signing key (gpg --list-secret-keys or SSH key) is available when SPIRAL_COMMIT_SIGNING is set
A failed signing attempt aborts the commit with a clear error rather than committing unsigned
technicalNotes: Git commit signing docs: https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Signing-Your-Work
SSH signing requires git >= 2.34: https://calebhearth.com/sign-git-with-ssh
Pass signing config via -c flags rather than modifying .git/config to keep it ephemeral

stories.title: Add GitHub Actions job summary with per-story results table on each CI run
stories.description: CI runs currently produce pass/fail status with no structured summary visible in the GitHub UI. Writing a Markdown summary to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY with a table of story IDs, statuses, token costs, and durations gives reviewers an at-a-glance view of each iteration's output directly on the Actions run page, without needing to parse raw log lines.
acceptanceCriteria: The CI workflow appends a Markdown table to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY after each spiral run
Table columns: Story ID, Title, Status (pass/fail/skip), Duration (s), Token Cost ($)
A summary footer shows total stories run, total cost, and total duration
The summary step runs even if earlier steps fail (using 'if: always()')
Summary size stays under 1 MiB (enforced by truncating to top 200 stories if needed)
technicalNotes: GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY docs: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-commands
GitHub Flavored Markdown is supported; tables, bold, and checkboxes all render
Generate summary from prd.json using jq or Python after each spiral iteration

stories.title: Use jq --stream for prd.json parsing to support files exceeding 10 MB
stories.description: As Spiral accumulates hundreds of stories with embedded LLM outputs, prd.json can grow past 10 MB. jq's default mode reads the entire file into memory; on constrained CI runners this causes OOM kills. Migrating prd.json queries in shell scripts to jq --stream mode (combined with fromstream/truncate_stream) enables memory-efficient extraction without loading the full document.
acceptanceCriteria: All jq invocations in spiral.sh and ralph.sh that read prd.json are audited; those reading top-level arrays are migrated to --stream mode
A test script generates a synthetic 15 MB prd.json and verifies jq --stream extraction completes under 512 MB RSS
Streaming queries use compact output (-c) to reduce intermediate allocation
A comment in the script explains why --stream is used, for maintainability
technicalNotes: jq streaming tutorial: https://devblog.songkick.com/parsing-ginormous-json-files-via-streaming-be6561ea8671
Pattern: jq -cn --stream 'fromstream(1|truncate_stream(.,1))' prd.json | jq 'select(.id=="US-123")'
jq 1.8.1 is the recommended version in 2026

stories.title: Add bats-assert and bats-support libraries to existing bats test suite
stories.description: The existing bats tests use raw bash assertions ([ ... ] with manual error messages), which produce cryptic output on failure. The bats-assert and bats-support helper libraries provide readable assertion functions (assert_output, assert_line, assert_success, refute_output) that emit diff-style failure messages. Adopting them improves test maintainability and makes CI failure output actionable without running locally.
acceptanceCriteria: bats-assert and bats-support are added as git submodules or npm devDependencies in the test directory
All existing bats tests are migrated to use assert_output / assert_success / assert_failure
At least one new test uses assert_line to check specific lines in multi-line output
CI installs bats helper libraries as part of the test setup step
Test failure output in CI shows the expected vs actual diff without additional tooling
technicalNotes: bats-core repo: https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core
bats-assert/bats-support are sub-projects under the bats-core GitHub org
Install via: git submodule add https://github.com/bats-core/bats-assert test/lib/bats-assert

stories.title: Add per-job GitHub Actions cache for uv/pip deps and pre-commit hooks
stories.description: CI jobs that reinstall Python dependencies and pre-commit environments from scratch on every run waste 2-5 minutes per run. Adding actions/cache steps keyed on the uv.lock (or requirements.txt) hash for Python deps and on the pre-commit config hash for hook environments eliminates these redundant installs, directly reducing CI cost and wait time.
acceptanceCriteria: A cache step with key '${{ hashFiles("**/uv.lock") }}' wraps Python dependency install in all CI jobs
Pre-commit hook environments are cached with key '${{ hashFiles(".pre-commit-config.yaml") }}'
Cache restore-keys provide fallback to nearest ancestor cache on miss
CI run duration is measured before and after; at least 2 minutes saved on warm runs
Cache invalidation is documented: changing uv.lock or pre-commit config busts the respective cache
technicalNotes: actions/cache v4 is required (v2/v3 deprecated Feb 2025): https://github.com/actions/cache
uv has its own cache dir (~/.cache/uv); key on uv.lock for lockfile-based installs
Pre-commit cache dir: ~/.cache/pre-commit; separate cache key from Python deps

stories.title: Structure bats tests to source functions under test for true unit coverage
stories.description: Current bats tests execute shell scripts as black boxes, meaning individual functions cannot be tested in isolation. Refactoring scripts to guard direct execution with 'if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]' allows bats tests to source the script and call individual functions, enabling true unit testing of helpers like worktree_prune, cost_check, and lock_cleanup with fine-grained assertions.
acceptanceCriteria: All major shell scripts (spiral.sh, ralph.sh, and key utility scripts) are refactored with BASH_SOURCE guard around their main execution block
At least 5 internal helper functions have dedicated bats unit tests that source the script and call the function directly
Existing integration-style bats tests continue to pass unchanged
A new 'unit' test suite target runs only the function-level tests (fast, no side effects)
CI runs both unit and integration bats suites and reports results separately
technicalNotes: BASH_SOURCE guard pattern: https://www.code-sage.com/blog/devops/2024/10/26/Automated-Testing-for-BASH-with-BATS.html
Move main logic to run_main() function, guard with: if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "${0}" ]]; then run_main "$@"; fi
Use bats-mock (https://github.com/grayhemp/bats-mock) to stub external commands like git, curl, jq

stories.title: Add tool parameter semantic validation before LLM-directed tool calls
stories.description: Agent tool failures are the most common failure mode in complex scenarios, often caused by incorrect parameter mapping. Before executing tool calls in ralph.sh, a validation layer checks parameter types and semantics against a tool schema registry, surfacing parameter errors before they cause hard-to-debug downstream failures.
acceptanceCriteria: A .spiral/tool-schema.json file defines expected parameter types for the top 10 tools invoked by workers (git, python, bats, jq, curl)
ralph.sh validates extracted tool call parameters against the schema before execution
Invalid parameters produce a structured error logged to checkpoint under _toolErrors: {tool, parameter, expected, received, timestamp}
A bats test verifies that a malformed tool call is caught at the validation layer and not executed
Schema validation adds no more than 50ms overhead per tool call
technicalNotes: Tools pillar finding: 'incorrect parameter mapping (region name vs. instance ID)' is the most common tool failure mode (arxiv 2512.12791)
Keep validation in bash/python (deterministic) not LLM to avoid recursive validation cost
Start with top 5 tools: git subcommand validation, python module paths, bats test file existence checks

stories.title: Add production failure telemetry feedback loop for prompt improvement
stories.description: Failed stories and low-quality phase outputs contain signal for improving system prompts and hints. After each iteration, a script extracts failure patterns from checkpoint data and appends structured feedback to a prompt-improvements log, creating a closed-loop system where production failures drive prompt iteration.
acceptanceCriteria: After each iteration completes, analyze_failures.py scans checkpoints of failed stories and extracts common failure patterns (tool errors, policy violations, low quality scores, context incomplete)
Patterns are written to .spiral/prompt-improvements.jsonl: {storyId, phase, failureCategory, suggestedHint, timestamp}
The dashboard displays a 'Top failure patterns this iteration' section sourced from this log
At least 4 distinct failure categories are recognized: tool_error, policy_violation, context_incomplete, quality_low
A bats test verifies analyze_failures.py correctly categorizes a set of fixture checkpoint files
technicalNotes: InsightFinder pattern: 'production telemetry as the richest input stream for improvement, converting production evidence into training data'
analyze_failures.py is read-only — it must not modify prd.json or checkpoint files
Run analyze_failures.py automatically at the end of each iteration, after Gate phase completes

stories.title: Implement human-in-the-loop approval gate for stories marked sensitive
stories.description: Some stories touch sensitive areas (database migrations, auth, public APIs) where autonomous execution without human review is unacceptable. A 'requiresApproval' flag pauses the worker after Phase I and signals for human approval before Phase V begins, enabling selective oversight without blocking all stories.
acceptanceCriteria: prd.json stories support a boolean 'requiresApproval' field
When a story with requiresApproval:true completes Phase I, the worker writes .spiral/pending-approvals/STORY_ID.json and pauses
A 'spiral approve STORY_ID' command creates .spiral/approvals/STORY_ID.approved to unblock the worker
Pending approvals appear prominently in the dashboard with elapsed wait time
If no approval is received within SPIRAL_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT (default 24h), the story is marked timed_out_awaiting_approval
technicalNotes: Vellum 2025: 'set checkpoints to wait for human approval before continuing' — approval gates for critical workflow junctures
martinfowler.com: 'human in the loop to supervise generation remains essential' for production code changes in sensitive areas
File-based signaling avoids requiring a running web server; poll interval configurable via SPIRAL_APPROVAL_POLL_INTERVAL

stories.title: Add living PRD changelog tracking story field mutations with author and reason
stories.description: prd.json is modified by multiple scripts with no audit trail. A changelog section tracks every mutation (status change, field edit, new story added) with timestamp, author script, and reason, enabling teams to understand how the backlog evolved and debug unexpected state transitions.
acceptanceCriteria: prd.json gains a top-level '_changelog' array where each entry has {timestamp, storyId, field, oldValue, newValue, author, reason}
All Python scripts that write to prd.json append a changelog entry for every field they modify
The changelog is append-only; only 'spiral changelog clear' may truncate it
A 'spiral changelog STORY_ID' command prints the full mutation history for a specific story
A bats test verifies that a status change from 'pending' to 'in_progress' generates a correctly structured changelog entry
technicalNotes: Modern PRD best practice 2025: 'utilize a robust system to manage document versions and track changes; avoid silent revisions that create confusion' (Atlassian/Aha.io)
Changelog differs from prd.json backup (already covered): it tracks field-level diffs, not file snapshots
Keep changelog entries compact: max 500 chars for reason field; truncate oldValue/newValue for array fields

stories.title: Tune parallel worker concurrency by operation type (CPU vs network vs disk)
stories.description: SPIRAL launches all workers with the same parallelism setting regardless of operation type, causing I/O thrashing on disk-intensive phases. Tuning concurrency by operation type prevents saturation and improves overall throughput by matching parallelism to the bottleneck resource.
acceptanceCriteria: Three separate env vars replace a single SPIRAL_WORKER_COUNT: SPIRAL_CPU_WORKERS (default: nproc), SPIRAL_NET_WORKERS (default: 4), SPIRAL_DISK_WORKERS (default: 2)
spiral.sh selects the appropriate limit by phase: Phase R (network, SPIRAL_NET_WORKERS), Phase I/V (CPU, SPIRAL_CPU_WORKERS), Phase M (disk, SPIRAL_DISK_WORKERS)
The active concurrency limit is logged at phase start: 'Launching N workers (network phase cap)'
A bats test verifies no more than SPIRAL_NET_WORKERS workers run concurrently during Phase R
Backward compatibility: setting SPIRAL_WORKER_COUNT still applies as a cap across all three limits
technicalNotes: gitcheatsheet.dev: 'CPU-bound: match parallelism to core count; Network: limit to 2-4 workers regardless of cores; Disk-bound: restrict to 1-2 workers to prevent I/O thrashing'
Benchmark: four parallel workers reduced test execution from 12 minutes to 5 minutes (58% reduction)
Phase classification: R=network, I=CPU+disk, V=CPU, M=disk

stories.title: Add dashboard story changelog drilldown view from prd.json _changelog
stories.description: Reconstruct the full lifecycle of any story in the dashboard from _changelog entries, showing every status change, field edit, and retry with timestamps and the responsible script. This enables operators to audit why a story ended up in its current state without digging through raw JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: The dashboard's per-story drilldown page includes a 'Story Changelog' tab sourced from prd.json._changelog filtered to that storyId
Each changelog entry is rendered as a timeline row: timestamp, changed field, old→new value, author script
The timeline is sorted chronologically and supports filtering by field name
A 'copy as markdown' button exports the story changelog as a markdown table
The changelog tab loads within 500ms even for stories with 100+ changelog entries
technicalNotes: Depends on the 'Add living PRD changelog tracking story field mutations' story for the _changelog field
Render using the existing HTML details element pattern already in the dashboard codebase
Filter implementation: client-side JavaScript, no additional server endpoints required

stories.title: Instrument worker phase transitions with OTel gen_ai.agent spans
stories.description: The existing OTel integration emits token-level gen_ai.usage.* counters but does not model each worker as a traceable agent entity with phase-level spans. Adopting the OpenTelemetry GenAI agent span conventions (gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.agent.id, invoke_agent span names) lets distributed tracing tools reconstruct the full R-I-V-T-M-G lifecycle per story as a trace tree, enabling root-cause analysis of slow or failing phases.
acceptanceCriteria: Each worker emits a root span named 'invoke_agent {worker-name}' with gen_ai.agent.id set to the worker ID and gen_ai.agent.name set to 'spiral-worker'
Each phase (R, I, V, T, M, G) is a child span named '{phase}-phase {story-id}' with gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.request.model attributes
gen_ai.conversation.id is set to the story ID to correlate all phases of a story across the trace
Spans are exported via OTLP to the endpoint configured in OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
The existing otel_run_context.json is updated to include the trace ID and agent span ID for cross-referencing
A bats test verifies that span JSON output contains all required gen_ai.agent.* attributes
technicalNotes: OTel GenAI agent span spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/
Required attributes: gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.provider.name; conditionally required: gen_ai.agent.name, gen_ai.agent.id
gen_ai.conversation.id maps naturally to prd.json story ID for full-trace correlation
Use opentelemetry-sdk Python package in spiral_dashboard.py or a separate otel_emitter.py helper

stories.title: Add gen_ai.client.operation.duration histogram for per-phase LLM latency
stories.description: The OTel GenAI metrics specification defines gen_ai.client.operation.duration (histogram, seconds) and gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token as standard latency metrics, but SPIRAL currently only emits token count counters. Adding latency histograms per phase and model gives operators percentile-level visibility (p50/p95/p99) into which phases are slowest, enabling targeted prompt or model optimisation.
acceptanceCriteria: gen_ai.client.operation.duration histogram is emitted for each LLM call with gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.request.model, and gen_ai.provider.name attributes
gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token is recorded for streaming responses where the first chunk timestamp is measurable
Metrics are exported alongside existing token counters via the same OTLP endpoint
spiral_dashboard.py displays p50 and p95 phase latency in the story detail panel
A unit test asserts that the histogram is updated on each simulated LLM call with the correct attribute set
technicalNotes: OTel GenAI metrics spec: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-metrics/
gen_ai.client.operation.duration is Histogram with unit 's' and status Required
gen_ai.server.time_to_first_token is Histogram with unit 's' and status Recommended
Use opentelemetry-sdk MeterProvider; record start/end timestamps around each API call

stories.title: Add per-worktree git config isolation to stamp AI commits with worker identity
stories.description: Worker worktrees inherit the global git user.name and user.email, meaning AI-generated commits appear attributed to the human developer's identity. Setting a per-worktree git config that stamps commits as a distinct SPIRAL worker identity provides clear audit trails distinguishing AI commits from human commits and prevents accidental exposure of developer PII in public repositories.
acceptanceCriteria: When spiral.sh creates a worktree, it immediately runs 'git -C <worktree-path> config user.name' and 'git -C <worktree-path> config user.email' scoped to that worktree only
Default values are configurable via SPIRAL_WORKER_GIT_NAME (default: 'SPIRAL Worker') and SPIRAL_WORKER_GIT_EMAIL (default: 'spiral-worker@localhost')
The trailer 'AI-Generated-By: SPIRAL/<worker-id>' is appended to all AI-authored commit messages via git interpret-trailers
A bats test checks that commits made from a worker worktree carry the worker identity, not the global git config values
The spiral status output shows the git author identity used per active worker
technicalNotes: Use 'git -C <path> config user.name <value>' to set config local to the worktree (not --global)
Git worktrees share .git objects but each has its own config layer via the worktree-specific gitdir
AI-Generated-By trailer follows Git trailer convention (RFC-compliant key: value format)
Reference: https://medium.com/@richardhightower/git-worktree-isolation-in-claude-code-parallel-development-without-the-chaos-262e12b85cc5

stories.title: Compute and store story quality score at ingestion based on acceptance criteria richness
stories.description: Stories enter the queue with wildly varying acceptance criteria quality — some have zero testable criteria, others contain only vague phrases like 'works correctly'. A quality scorer runs at ingestion time and assigns a 0-100 score based on measurable signals: number of acceptance criteria, presence of specific numeric thresholds, absence of vague language, and completeness of technicalNotes. Low-quality stories are flagged before any worker is assigned.
acceptanceCriteria: A score_story_quality(story) function returns a QualityScore with: total (0-100), breakdown { criteria_count_pts, specificity_pts, measurability_pts, technical_notes_pts, source_pts }, and issues list

Scoring: +20 for >= 3 acceptance criteria; +5 per criterion containing a number/threshold/percentage (up to +20); -10 per criterion containing a vague term ('works', 'correctly', 'properly', 'good', 'better', 'appropriate'); +20 for non-empty technicalNotes; +20 for a source URL
Stories with quality score < 40 are assigned status 'needs-refinement' and are not dispatched to workers
spiral status shows a quality score column (numeric, colour-coded) per story
The _qualityScore field is written to prd.json as an annotation field not editable by humans
A unit test asserts a story with no acceptance criteria and only vague language scores below 40
technicalNotes: Vague term list: ['works', 'correctly', 'properly', 'good', 'better', 'nice', 'easy', 'simple', 'appropriate', 'reasonable']
Use regex r'\b\d+(\.\d+)?\s*(ms|MB|GB|%|s|seconds|tokens|requests)\b' to detect measurable thresholds
_qualityScore is stored alongside existing annotation fields like _humanNotes and _changelog
Reference quality benchmarking from JSONSchemaBench: https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10868v3

stories.title: Implement contract-based integration tests for each SPIRAL phase boundary
stories.description: Phase handoffs in SPIRAL (Phase R output to Phase I input, Phase V output to Gate decision) are untested end-to-end; a bug in the Phase R output format silently breaks Phase I without a clear error. Contract-style integration tests with bats exercise each of the six phase boundaries using fixture inputs and assert the output contract (schema and key fields), catching regressions before they reach production workers.
acceptanceCriteria: A test/integration/ directory contains bats tests for each of the 6 phase transitions: R->I, I->V, V->T, T->M, M->G, G->done
Each test sources a fixture JSON file (test/fixtures/phase_<N>_output.json) as input to the next phase and asserts the output satisfies the phase's documented contract
Contract assertions include: correct exit code, expected output file(s) created, required JSON keys present, status field updated correctly in prd.json
Tests use bats-assert for readable assertion failures (assert_output, assert_file_exists)
CI runs the integration tests in a dedicated matrix job after unit tests pass
A test specifically verifies that a malformed Phase R output missing the researchSummary key causes Phase I to exit with code 1 and a descriptive error message
technicalNotes: Contract testing concept: https://pactflow.io/blog/ai-automation-part-1/
bats-assert + bats-support: https://github.com/bats-core/bats-assert
Fixture files avoid LLM calls in CI by mocking API endpoints with environment variable stubs
Phase contracts should be codified as JSON Schema in test/contracts/phase_<N>_contract.json

stories.title: Add role-based story assignment and approval workflow for multi-user teams
stories.description: SPIRAL is currently single-operator; all stories are owned by the same author and all workers run under the same credentials. A lightweight role system (owner, reviewer, operator) in prd.json stories enables team use: owners author stories, reviewers approve quality scores before dispatch, and operators monitor workers — providing the audit trail and access boundaries that enterprise team adoption requires.
acceptanceCriteria: prd.json stories gain three new optional fields: _assignedTo (string, GitHub username), _reviewedBy (string, GitHub username), _approvalStatus (enum: pending|approved|rejected)
spiral assign <story-id> <username> sets _assignedTo and records the action in _changelog with timestamp and actor
spiral approve <story-id> sets _reviewedBy to SPIRAL_USER env var and changes _approvalStatus to 'approved', enabling dispatch
Stories with quality score < 40 are automatically set to _approvalStatus 'pending' and require explicit 'spiral approve' before worker dispatch
A webhook event is emitted to SPIRAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK when _approvalStatus changes, including story ID, reviewer, verdict, and timestamp
The spiral status table shows _assignedTo and _approvalStatus columns when SPIRAL_SHOW_TEAM_COLUMNS=true
technicalNotes: Multiplayer AI pattern: permission-aware behavior respecting team boundaries — https://thenewstack.io/the-next-era-of-ai-from-single-user-to-team-collaboration/
SPIRAL_USER env var defaults to output of 'git config user.name'
Role enforcement is advisory (logged, not cryptographically enforced) in v1; pairs with HMAC webhook signing for tamper-evidence
Integrates with existing _humanNotes and _changelog annotation fields already in prd.json schema

stories.title: Generate Markdown documentation stubs and CHANGELOG entries on Gate pass
stories.description: Every story that passes the Gate represents a completed, tested feature whose documentation (README sections, changelog entries) is never automatically created. Generating documentation stubs from the story's title, description, acceptanceCriteria, and technicalNotes at Gate-pass time creates a reviewable first-draft, reducing documentation debt without requiring an additional LLM call.
acceptanceCriteria: When a story transitions to status 'merged', a generate_docs() function creates docs/stories/<story-id>.md containing: title as H1, description, acceptanceCriteria as a checkbox list, and technicalNotes as a code-fenced list
A CHANGELOG.md entry is appended in Keep a Changelog format: '### Added\n- <story-title> (<story-id>)'
Generated files are committed in the merge commit attributed to the SPIRAL worker identity with the AI-Generated-By trailer
SPIRAL_GENERATE_DOCS=false env var disables generation for development environments
A bats test verifies that running the Gate-pass hook on a fixture story produces the expected Markdown file with all required sections present
Generated stubs include a header comment: '<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by SPIRAL <story-id> — review before finalising -->'
technicalNotes: Keep a Changelog format: https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/
Use Python string templates or Jinja2 for Markdown generation; no external LLM call needed
Commit with git interpret-trailers to append 'AI-Generated-By: SPIRAL/<story-id>'
docs/stories/ directory follows the same pattern as planned ADR stubs for architectural decisions

stories.title: Add epic-level hierarchical orchestration with supervisor worker and DAG dispatch
stories.description: Large epics in prd.json have no structural relationship to their child stories; a single orchestrator dispatches all stories without priority awareness within an epic. A hierarchical orchestration mode assigns one supervisor worker per epic that reads the dependency graph, orders sub-stories topologically, and dispatches sub-workers in sequence or parallel — matching the NeurIPS 2025 finding that learned task routing outperforms fixed pipelines by structuring work before distributing it.
acceptanceCriteria: prd.json stories gain an optional _epicId field; stories sharing an _epicId form an epic group
When SPIRAL_HIERARCHICAL_MODE=true, spiral.sh creates one supervisor process per epic before dispatching sub-workers
The supervisor builds a dependency DAG from stories' dependencies[] fields using topological sort and dispatches sub-workers in dependency order
Sub-worker progress is reported back to the supervisor, which updates the epic-level status in prd.json
If a sub-worker fails, the supervisor applies existing dead-letter queue logic and continues dispatching independent stories in the epic
spiral status shows epics as collapsible groups with aggregate progress displayed as 'X/N stories done'
technicalNotes: NeurIPS 2025 dynamic orchestration: learned task routing outperforms fixed multi-agent pipelines — https://blog.promptlayer.com/multi-agent-evolving-orchestration/
Orchestrator-Worker pattern: https://gurusup.com/blog/agent-orchestration-patterns — central coordinator with fan-out to workers
Topological sort: Python graphlib.TopologicalSorter (stdlib, Python 3.9+) for the dependency DAG
Supervisor state persisted to .spiral/workers/<epic-id>/supervisor_state.json for crash recovery

stories.title: Add OpenMetrics /metrics HTTP endpoint to spiral_dashboard.py
stories.description: Expose a Prometheus-compatible OpenMetrics endpoint at /metrics in spiral_dashboard.py so external monitoring stacks (Grafana, Victoria Metrics) can scrape SPIRAL runtime state. Metrics should include story counts by status, cumulative API cost, iteration count, and active worker count.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /metrics returns HTTP 200 with Content-Type: application/openmetrics-text; charset=utf-8
Response includes gauges for spiral_stories_total{status=pending|passed|failed|skipped}, spiral_cost_total_usd, spiral_iteration_count, spiral_workers_active
Metrics update in real time without requiring a dashboard restart
Endpoint is accessible when SPIRAL_DASHBOARD_PORT is set and dashboard is running
prometheus_client Python package is used via openmetrics exposition module
technicalNotes: Use prometheus_client.openmetrics.exposition.generate_latest() for correct Content-Type header
Register a CollectorRegistry and pass it to the Flask/FastAPI route handler
OpenMetrics is a GA CNCF standard (2023); legacy Prometheus text format is deprecated for new consumers
Reference: https://github.com/prometheus/client_python/blob/master/prometheus_client/openmetrics/exposition.py

stories.title: Validate all phase output JSON files with versioned Pydantic v2 models
stories.description: Replace ad-hoc JSON key checks in spiral.sh with Pydantic v2 models for each phase output file (_research_output.json, _validated_stories.json, _test_stories_output.json). Each model carries a schema_version field and auto-migrates older payloads on load, preventing silent data corruption from schema drift.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/schemas.py defines Pydantic v2 BaseModel subclasses for ResearchOutput, ValidatedStories, and TestStoriesOutput
Each model has a schema_version: int field (default=1); a load_and_migrate() factory handles older versions
Loading a phase output file with an unrecognized schema_version raises a MigrationError with the version number
All existing Python modules that read phase output files use the new schema models
mypy --strict passes for lib/schemas.py with no type: ignore suppressions
technicalNotes: Pydantic v2 model_config = ConfigDict(extra='ignore') allows forward compatibility with unknown fields
Use Annotated[int, Field(ge=1)] for schema_version to enforce valid version numbers
V1 to V2 field renames handled via @model_validator(mode='before') in the Pydantic model
Reference: https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/migration/ — model_config and @model_validator patterns

stories.title: Multi-model consensus voting for stories tagged estimatedComplexity=large
stories.description: For stories with estimatedComplexity=large, run Phase I implementation with two different models in parallel and compare outputs. If both implementations pass Phase V, accept the one with higher test coverage delta. If they disagree, escalate to the interactive gate for human resolution.
acceptanceCriteria: When SPIRAL_CONSENSUS_ENABLED=true, stories with estimatedComplexity=large spawn two parallel workers with different models
Both worker outputs are validated independently by SPIRAL_VALIDATE_CMD
If both pass, the implementation with higher line coverage delta is promoted
If only one passes, that implementation is accepted automatically
If both fail, the story is retried via normal retry logic; consensus result is logged to results.tsv as a consensus_result column
SPIRAL_CONSENSUS_MODELS env var specifies the two models (default: claude-sonnet-4-5,claude-opus-4-5)
technicalNotes: Majority voting with 2 agents requires a tie-breaker (coverage delta); 3-agent pools self-resolve via majority vote
Consensus doubles token cost for large stories; SPIRAL_COST_CEILING should account for this when SPIRAL_CONSENSUS_ENABLED=true
Debate-based consensus (ACL 2025) produces more accurate results but increases latency; simple output comparison is sufficient for Phase I
Reference: https://galileo.ai/blog/multi-agent-coordination-strategies

stories.title: Add cyclomatic complexity gate: warn when story implementation exceeds threshold
stories.description: After Phase I implementation, run a cyclomatic complexity analysis using radon on all Python files modified by the story. If any function exceeds SPIRAL_MAX_CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY (default: 10), emit a warning to spiral_events.jsonl. When SPIRAL_COMPLEXITY_HARD_GATE=true, treat exceedance as a story failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase I post-step runs 'radon cc -s -j <changed_files>' on modified Python files
Functions with complexity > SPIRAL_MAX_CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY are logged as warnings in spiral_events.jsonl with story_id and file:line
When SPIRAL_COMPLEXITY_HARD_GATE=true, the story is flagged as failed and decomposition is triggered
SPIRAL_MAX_CYCLOMATIC_COMPLEXITY defaults to 10 per McCabe's recommended threshold
Complexity gate is skipped if radon is not installed, with a one-time advisory message
technicalNotes: radon is installable via 'uv pip install radon'; outputs JSON with 'radon cc -j'
McCabe's original paper (1976) recommends complexity <= 10 as the threshold for maintainable code
Run only on files in the story's filesTouch list to avoid scanning unrelated files
Reference: https://radon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/intro.html

stories.title: Integration test for Phase R to M pipeline with VCR-recorded API responses
stories.description: Add a pytest integration test that exercises the full Phase R (research output parsing) through Phase S (validation) through Phase M (merge) pipeline using pre-recorded API responses via vcrpy cassettes. This catches regressions in JSON parsing, schema validation, and deduplication logic without live API calls.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_phase_rsm_integration.py runs the Phase R output parser, Phase S validator, and Phase M merger in sequence
All HTTP calls are intercepted by vcrpy cassettes stored in tests/fixtures/cassettes/
Test verifies that a known research output containing duplicates results in the correctly deduplicated stories in prd.json
Test verifies that a research output with schema violations is rejected before merge
Test runs in CI without network access (cassettes are committed to the repo)
Test is marked @pytest.mark.integration and excluded from fast unit test run
technicalNotes: vcrpy records and replays HTTP interactions; cassettes are YAML files in tests/fixtures/cassettes/
Use @pytest.fixture with vcr.use_cassette() decorator for clean test isolation
Set cassette record_mode='none' in CI to prevent accidental live API calls
Reference: https://vcrpy.readthedocs.io/en/latest/

stories.title: Phase S completeness gate: reject stories below stored _qualityScore threshold
stories.description: Extend Phase S (Story Validate) to use the _qualityScore field (computed at ingestion) as a hard gate. Stories below SPIRAL_MIN_STORY_QUALITY (default: 0.5) are rejected from the merge batch with a structured rejection reason, preventing low-quality stories from entering the implementation queue.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase S reads _qualityScore from each candidate story; stories with _qualityScore < SPIRAL_MIN_STORY_QUALITY are dropped
Rejection reason 'quality_score_below_threshold' is written to the story's _rejectionReason field
Rejection count and score distribution are emitted to spiral_events.jsonl as a phase_s_summary event
SPIRAL_MIN_STORY_QUALITY defaults to 0.5; setting it to 0.0 disables the gate
Stories without a _qualityScore field (e.g., seed stories) bypass this gate entirely
technicalNotes: _qualityScore is computed by the pending 'Compute and store story quality score at ingestion' story
Gate should run after constitution/goal/dedup checks but before merge, as the last Phase S filter
Log rejected stories to .spiral/rejected_stories.jsonl for operator review
Depends on: Compute and store story quality score at ingestion based on acceptance criteria richness

stories.title: Watch plugin.toml for changes and hot-reload plugins without restarting spiral.sh
stories.description: Add between-iteration mtime checking for plugin.toml and plugin script files. When a change is detected, reload only the affected plugin hooks so operators can iterate on plugins without restarting long-running SPIRAL sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh sources plugin hooks at the start of each phase iteration, not once at startup
When plugin.toml or a referenced script file mtime changes, a [plugin-reload] entry appears in spiral_events.jsonl
Reloading a plugin with a syntax error logs the error and skips the hook without aborting the iteration
Plugin hot-reload is enabled by default; disabled via SPIRAL_PLUGIN_HOT_RELOAD=false
Unit test verifies that modifying a plugin script between iterations causes the new version to be sourced
technicalNotes: In bash, store plugin file mtimes in an associative array and compare at each iteration start using 'stat -c %Y'
Avoid inotify in bash on Windows — mtime polling every iteration is sufficient for SPIRAL's loop cadence
Python watchdog library provides cross-platform inotify/FSEvents/kqueue file watching if a Python-based reload daemon is preferred
Reference: https://python-watchdog.readthedocs.io/en/stable/

stories.title: Track ralph/CLAUDE.md prompt version as content hash in results.tsv
stories.description: Compute a short SHA-256 hash of the ralph/CLAUDE.md system prompt at the start of each SPIRAL run and record it as a prompt_version column in results.tsv and as a field in _iteration_summary.json. This enables post-hoc analysis of which prompt version produced better story pass rates.
acceptanceCriteria: spiral.sh computes PROMPT_VERSION=$(sha256sum ralph/CLAUDE.md | cut -c1-8) at startup
results.tsv gains a prompt_version column containing the 8-char hash for every story attempt row
_iteration_summary.json includes a prompt_version field
When ralph/CLAUDE.md has uncommitted changes, prompt_version is suffixed with '-dirty'
Unit test verifies that two different CLAUDE.md contents produce different hash values
technicalNotes: sha256sum is available in Git Bash on Windows; use certutil -hashfile on CMD as fallback
Truncate to 8 chars (like git short SHA) for readability in the TSV column
Enables pandas groupby analysis: df.groupby('prompt_version')['status'].value_counts() shows pass rate per prompt version
Reference: prompt versioning best practices — https://www.promptingguide.ai/

stories.title: Wizard: probe available Claude models via API before presenting routing configuration
stories.description: During setup wizard initialization, call the Anthropic Models API to fetch the list of models accessible with the user's API key. Present only available models in routing configuration questions, preventing misconfiguration errors from referencing unavailable or deprecated model IDs.
acceptanceCriteria: Wizard calls GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models before presenting the model routing question
Only claude-* models returned by the API are shown as selectable options
If the API call fails, wizard falls back to a hardcoded model list with a visible warning
Fetched model list is cached in .spiral/available_models.json and reused for 24 hours
technicalNotes: Use existing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var for authentication
Filter response to models where id starts with 'claude-' to exclude experimental IDs
Implement as lib/probe_models.py using urllib (no extra deps)

stories.title: Pre-warm git worktrees during Phase M to reduce Phase I startup latency
stories.description: Worker git worktrees are currently created on-demand at Phase I startup, adding sequential latency before any implementation work begins. Pre-create worktrees in background subprocesses during the lighter Phase M merge step so Phase I workers can start immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Worktree creation is triggered as a background subprocess at the end of Phase M
Phase I waits for pre-warm completion before dispatching workers, with a 30-second timeout fallback
SPIRAL_PREWARM_WORKTREES=false disables pre-warming (default: true)
Pre-warm failure falls back gracefully to on-demand creation without aborting Phase I
Pre-warm skips creation for worktrees that already exist from a prior run
technicalNotes: Background creation: git worktree add .spiral-workers/worker-N <branch> then disown
Coordination signal: write .spiral/_prewarm_ready when all N worktrees are confirmed present
Respect existing disk space preflight check before initiating pre-warm

stories.title: Add deterministic LLM response cache keyed by prompt hash for story replays
stories.description: Cache LLM API responses for identical (model + prompt) pairs using a SHA-256 hash key stored in `.spiral/llm_cache/`. On retry or explicit replay, return the cached response instead of a live API call, reducing cost and latency for deterministic debugging sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: Cache key = SHA-256(model_id + full_prompt_text); stored in .spiral/llm_cache/<hash>.json
A cache hit is logged to spiral_events.jsonl as {event: llm_cache_hit, story_id, model}
SPIRAL_LLM_CACHE_ENABLED=true enables caching (default: false for live accuracy)
Cache entries are auto-purged after SPIRAL_LLM_CACHE_TTL_HOURS (default: 24)
SPIRAL_CACHE_INVALIDATE=STORY_ID env var forces cache bypass for a specific story
technicalNotes: Distinct from .spiral/research_cache/ (HTTP responses) — this caches raw LLM API responses
Implement as lib/llm_cache.py with read_cache(key) and write_cache(key, response) functions
Disabled by default to avoid stale responses masking real behavior in production runs

stories.title: Add token usage percentile statistics (P50/P90/P99) to --cost-report output
stories.description: Extend cost reporting with per-model token usage percentile statistics computed from results.tsv. P50/P90/P99 token counts identify outlier stories that consume disproportionate context and should be targeted for story decomposition or context pruning.
acceptanceCriteria: --cost-report output includes a percentile table: model | p50_tokens | p90_tokens | p99_tokens | max_tokens
Percentiles are computed separately for input tokens and output tokens
Stories exceeding the P99 input token threshold are listed by ID in a 'token outliers' section
Percentile section is omitted gracefully when fewer than 10 data points exist per model
technicalNotes: Use Python statistics.quantiles() for percentile computation (stdlib, no extra deps)
Group by model column in results.tsv before computing statistics
Implement in lib/cost_report.py alongside the --cost-report story
